newsitem.title: USA: U.S. not accusing Cuba of breaking migration pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. not accusing Cuba of breaking migration pact.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it was not accusing Cuba of violating an agreement by jailing six would-be emigrants sent home by U.S. authorities and charged with commandeering a boat.
A Cuban court on Tuesday sentenced the six Cubans to terms ranging from eight to 20 years for hijacking a tugboat to try to travel to the United States, the Cuban news agency Prensa Latina said.

Under a 1995 agreement aimed at halting the flow of illegal rafters from Cuba, the United States undertook to return to Cuba boat people whom it intercepted at sea. Cuba pledged not to prosecute returnees as a direct consequence of their attempt to immigrate illegally.

But State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the agreement "does not provide immunity against prosecution for criminal offences, such as hijacking, which are committed before, or during or after the departure attempt".

"We have not accused (Cuba) of violating any agreement in this particular case," Burns told a news briefing. "I'm not saying that we support the actions either. I'm just saying we're not accusing them of violation."
Burns said eight to 20 year terms "would be consistent with the normal length of sentences in Cuban hijacking cases."

He said that since the repatriation of the six Cubans in May 1996, officers from the U.S. interest section in Havana had made regular visits to their families to monitor the progress of the case and ensure that no reprisals were taken against family members.
On Wednesday, the interest section delivered a diplomatic note to the Cuban government, asking for details of the verdict, he added.
Prensa Latina said the six convicted Cubans used a fake bomb, two revolvers and a knife to overpower the captain of the tugboat off the coast of eastern Holguin province in April 1996.
Under the 1995 agreement, the United States agreed to accept up to 20,000 Cubans a year who applied to emigrate through legal channels.
